37323.subject: Chemistry
37323.question_text: Which of the following ions is isoelectronic with neon? [\(_3\)Li, \(_9\)F, \(_{10}\)Ne, \(_{17}\)CI,\(_{19}\)K ]
37323.explanation:
Neon has electronic configuration of  2,8

\(_3\)Li\(^+\) has electronic configuration of  2 (because the + sign shows it has given out one electron from the initial 2, 1, and now has 2 with only one shell)

\(_9\)F\(^-\) has electronic configuration of  2, 8 (because the - sign shows it has accepted one electron and now the initial 2, 7, now becomes 2,8 with only 2 shells)

\(_{17}\)CI\(^-\) has electronic configuration of  2,8,8 (because the - sign shows it has accepted one electron and now the initial 2,8, 7,now becomes 2,8,8 with only 3 shells)

\(_{19}\)K\(^+\) has electronic configuration of  2,8,8(because the - sign shows it has given out one electron and now the initial 2,8,8,1 now becomes 2,8,8 with only 3 shells)

Among all the options above, the only one that has the same number of electrons (Isoelectronic) with Neon (2,8) is   \(_9\)F\(^-\) (2,8)

37348.subject: Chemistry
37348.question_text: How many molecules are there in 14 g of nitrogen at s.t.p.? [N = 14, Avogadro's constant = 6.02 x 10\(^{23}\) mol-1]
37348.explanation:
Given:

mass, m = 14g

Molar mass of N\(_2\) = 14 X 2 = 28g/mol

number of moles, n = ?

But n = \(\frac{m}{M}\) = \(\frac{14}{28}\) 

                       n = 0.5 mole

Also, recall that Number of moles = \(\frac{Number of Molecules}{Avogadro number}\)

                                                n  = \(\frac{N}{L}\)

                                                N = n x L

                                                   = 0.5 x 6.02 x  10\(^{23}\)

                                                   = 3.01 x 10\(^{23}\) molecules

37426.subject: Chemistry
37426.question_text: Which of the following noble gases has electronic structure similar to that of N in NH\(_3\)? [\(^{14}_7\)N]
37426.explanation: The nitrogen atom in ammonia NH\(_3\) has a similar outer shell configuration to Neon because it needs three more electrons to complete its outer shell. Hence, Nitrogen atom shares its three unpaired electrons with three covalent bonds.This configuration gives Nitrogen a stable octet of electrons, similar to the noble gas Neon, which also has a full outer energy level with eight eight electrons.
